## Findings
- claim-1: In degrees \(6,7,8,9,10\), claim-1 reports quotient free ranks \(1,1,2,1,1\), respectively, and no torsion. [artifact 621a26ec7b4419d76351b43e22fff9df644945c6458e2a531d2542a0819b6602]
- claim-2: Quotient rank and torsion do not determine ordered \(G_L\)-to-\(G_R\) transition matrices.
## Strategy
Let an ordered transition matrix satisfy
\[
[g_{L,r}]=\sum_c(T_d)_{r,c}[g_{R,c}].
\]
Claim-1 reports only
\[
(\operatorname{rank}Q_d,\operatorname{Tor}Q_d)=(1,0),(1,0),(2,0),(1,0),(1,0)
\]
for \(d=6,\ldots,10\), respectively; it contains no marked-basis coordinates.

To prove these invariants insufficient, take \(Q=\mathbb Z^2\) with \(G_L=(e_1,e_2)\). Both ordered bases
\[
G_R=(e_1,e_2),\qquad G_R'=(e_2,e_1)
\]
have identical quotient invariants \((\operatorname{rank}Q,\operatorname{Tor}Q)=(2,0)\), but their transition matrices are
\[
I_2,\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
with determinants \(1\) and \(-1\), respectively. Thus rank and torsion do not determine an ordered transition matrix.

Boundary cases: for \(Q=\mathbb Z\), changing the right basis from \((e)\) to \((-e)\) changes \(T=(1)\) to \(T=(-1)\), while invariants remain \((1,0)\). For \(Q=0\), both bases and the transition matrix are empty; \(T\) is \(0\times0\), with conventional determinant \(1\). This exceptional uniqueness does not supply transition data in positive rank.

Hence the scoped certificate is established.

## Gaps
None for this logical insufficiency certificate. It does not compute or certify the actual \(G_L\)-to-\(G_R\) matrices.

## Next
Any actual transition claim requires separate coordinate, determinant, or Smith witnesses.
